relevance_note: Six probands with familial LCAT deficiency are described individually with their LCAT mutations: 'Sequence analysis identified homozygous missense or nonsense mutations in four probands.'
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON, sliced Table I/II row segments from the Markdown lines (values checked against the tables) and verified every span verbatim. Labels: Table I/II identify each patient by the family letter (A, B, D, E) and C1/C2 for the two family C probands ('C1 and C2 refer to the two affected probands in family C'); these are used as the paper's own labels (Table I prints C1 as 'Cl'). Scope: the 43 relatives (23 genotypic heterozygotes, 20 unaffected; Table II heterozygous/unaffected rows) are reported only as family-level group means with n, without any individual-level detail, so they get no rows; cohort_size_as_stated = 6 patients (plus 43 relatives analysed). Variant strings: the Markdown prints '>' as '>'; values decode it to '>' while spans keep the Markdown text. The paper gives codon/amino-acid and nucleotide-triplet changes only (no c./p. HGVS, no transcript), so cdna/protein fields are null. Family B carries two missense changes (codons 93 and 158) on the same allele (cis); recorded as two variant rows. Table III is badly garbled by conversion (columns shifted, 'horn' for 'hom'); it was used only where a cell is legible in the person's own row (A 'hom', E 'hom'). Zygosity 'homozygous' for A, B, D, E rests on 'In four of the five families the patients were homozygous' together with family C being the stated compound-heterozygous exception. Table I symbols: '+' read as present; '-' is not defined in the legend, so '-' cells (A target cells, C2 proteinuria and renal disease) are not reported (A anemia is excluded from the text instead). E's renal disease cell '(+)*-' is ambiguous and not used. The legend footnote 'No target cells but otherwise irregularly shaped erythrocytes present' cannot be attached to a patient. C1's sex cell reads 'Im' (conversion artefact) and is recorded not reported. Ages at last evaluation come from Table I 'Age at examination'. Lab features (low HDL, increased unesterified cholesterol, increased cholesterol:ester ratio, LCAT activity <2, LCAT mass absent/reduced, no congenital heart disease) come from statements naming all probands/all six patients; per-person Table II values are added as detail. Plasma values such as apo A-I 36-48 mg/dl and triglycerides are printed but never called low/high by the authors for the patients, so the related checklist items are not reported. Mesangial proliferation (A, B), foam cells in D's kidney biopsy (site not stated), glomerular lipid accumulation (E) and D's hemodialysis were not mapped to narrower/broader checklist items. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27): A creatinine/creatinine clearance normal in 1985, E urea nitrogen, creatinine and creatinine clearance normal. Contradictions/discrepancies: A is '39-yr old' in Methods but 38 in Table I; B 'now 48 yr old' vs 47 in Table I; E '38-yr old' vs 39 in Table I; family C ancestry 'Italian and Dutch' in the text vs the title of reference 12 'Italian and Swedish descent'; E's family 'was not available for analysis' but the Discussion cites low HDL in 'several first degree relatives of the proband in family E'; Discussion says 'six different mutations ... in five patients' while seven changes on six alleles in six patients are described.
